transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-18
Start: 14:00 EST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Nora Black (Redwood CSM), Ava Rodrí guez (Verdant Head of ML), Mark Hollis (Verdant VP Product), Devin Park (Verdant SRE), Priya Iyer (Verdant Finance), Eli Thomson (Verdant Data Eng)

Summary (auto): QBR focused on cost optimization (rightsizing), reliability incidents in Nov, and roadmap alignment for Dedicated/private options. Agreed next steps on rightsizing proposal, latency bench, and budget confirmation.

[00:00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Samira from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Quick roll call — who we got?
[00:00:07] Ava: Ava here, hi all.
[00:00:09] Mark: Mark on Product.
[00:00:11] Devin: Devin, SRE.
[00:00:13] Priya: Priya from Finance.
[00:00:15] Eli: Eli, data eng.
[00:00:18] Samira: Great. Also with me are Liam Chen, our solutions engineer, and Nora Black, your CSM. We'll run through usage and cost trends, recent reliability items, then roadmap and rightsizing.
[00:00:30] Liam: quick FYI I'll jump into the latency/throughput stuff. Might mis-say some names, my notes can be messy.
[00:00:35] Nora: I'll capture action items.

[00:02:10] Samira: Ok first slide — usage trend. We see a steady 18% month-on-month growth in token consumption for the core inference routes, with embedding spikes for batch analytics. Priya, is the billing cadence monthly or do you budget quarterly?
[00:02:24] Priya: We budget quarterly but approvals come monthly. The November overrun surprised us, we need rightsizing if we want to hit our Q1 targets.
[00:02:35] Eli: small note — we kicked off a large batch embedding job that may have run longer than expected, that coupled with higher interactive traffic caused the spike.
[00:02:45] Samira: Got it — that's where a caching profile could help (prefix caching + TTL tweak). We can recommend a cache-first pattern for embeddings, and also look at switching some of the high-volume pipelines to a quantized model variant.

[00:06:12] Mark: On reliability — we had two incidents in November where tail latencies hit ~2.1s for gen endpoints. We saw some retries from the app. What's the mitigation surface?
[00:06:22] Liam: For tail latency you have a few levers: increase the Dedicated pool size, enable continuous batching, or allow a higher-quality quantization for baseline traffic. There's also prefix KV caching — though I keep seeing our notes saying K-V cash in previous docs — sorry for the typo. The other thing is routing: you can route internal traffic to a lower-cost variant and only route high-priority customer traffic to the lower-latency variant.
[00:06:45] Ava: can you quickly explain continuous batching again? Our engineers were confused between batching and queueing.
[00:06:51] Liam: Sure, continuous batching is an inference runtime technique that holds a tiny window of requests (milliseconds) and forms batches adaptively so throughput increases without large latency penalties. It's different from coarse queueing. In practice you set the max wait and max batch size in the route config.

[00:10:12] Devin: we ran into a problem where during peak we hit a soft quota and requests were shunted — the app retried aggressively and amplified. Is there a built-in backpressure or retry guidance?
[00:10:22] Nora: Yes, on the console you can set per-route rate limits and burst policies; plus we recommend client-side exponential backoff with jitter. We'll share a sample retry policy.
[00:10:30] Samira: Also there's an auto-fallback policy — if Dedicated capacity is constrained we can fallback to the hosted variant compatible with your pinned model. It costs more per token but avoids failures.

[00:12:55] Priya: cost question — what's the delta if we move 30% of traffic to Dedicated reserved vs keep hosted with burst?
[00:13:03] Samira: Short answer: Dedicated gives predictable unit cost and lower tail latency but requires a committed monthly spend. Hosted with burst is more elastic but unit cost per token is higher during peaks. I'll send a 30/60/90 rightsizing sheet with modeled scenarios.
[00:13:18] Priya: we need scenarios that show net savings over 6 and 12 months.

[00:15:40] Liam: small technical item — your current model in prod is a 24B dense model; we can offer a 16B quantized variant that keeps ~95% of quality on your eval for chat but drops compute by ~40%. We ran an internal eval — quality trade-off is there but acceptable for non-customer-facing analytic routes.
[00:15:58] Ava: what's the easiest path to test that?
[00:16:01] Liam: a canary route — create a weighted rollout and run the eval set. We'll show how to set up per-route rollouts in the console.

[00:20:06] Mark: reliability postmortem — Devin, can you summarize root cause?
[00:20:11] Devin: Sure. During the incident we saw a combo of a long-tail KV miss pattern for our prompt templates plus a surge in batch embeddings. The K-V layer in our service had a cache misconfiguration that caused extra compute. Also some of our regional routing sent traffic to a smaller pool in us-west-2.
[00:20:34] Samira: sounds like two prongs — application-level caching and the routing policy. We can help with recommended prefixes and an audit of route configs.

[00:24:50] Eli: question on observability — can we get per-request token breakdowns and cost attribution for a route? We need it to reconcile chargebacks across product teams.
[00:24:58] Nora: Yes, the Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route cost attribution, and you can export daily CSVs. We can enable longer retention for a fee.
[00:25:10] Priya: would prefer automated daily exports to our S3.
[00:25:14] Nora: we can add a deliverable to send a sample export and S3 ingestion guide.

[00:28:45] Samira: Let's touch roadmap — Verdant wants to expand the clinical summarization feature next quarter. How's the model pinning and rollout support?
[00:28:53] Liam: You can pin model versions per route and do targeted rollouts by user cohort. For clinical summarization I'd recommend a smaller quantized eval in staging, then a phased canary with fallbacks to the previous version. Also we have private deployment options if you need V-P-C peering and customer-managed KMS. Sorry I said V-P-C instead of VPC earlier.
[00:29:15] Ava: we'll likely need private deployment for compliance if we go wider with PHI. What compliance artifacts do you have?
[00:29:22] Samira: We maintain SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO docs, and can provide our SOC two and ISO attestation packages plus audit logs. On SSO we have SAML/Sammy L integrations and RBAC. We'll share the security pack link after the call.

[00:32:00] Mark: SLA expectations — can Dedicated give us an SLA for p99 latency?
[00:32:06] Liam: We guarantee uptime SLAs for Dedicated and we have latency targets in the contract for standard model families; p99 latency SLAs are available for committed tiers with the Atlas plan. We can surface the exact numbers in the contract appendix.

[00:35:10] Devin: technical ask — can you run a bench that reproduces our peak profile (mix of short gen requests and large embedding batches)? We need numbers to justify a Dedicated commit to procurement.
[00:35:21] Liam: yes, we'll run a 1000-concurrent microbench that simulates your route mix in staging. We'll share the scripts and raw results. Expect initial pass within two weeks.

[00:38:40] Priya: procurement timeline — if we decide to commit to Dedicated, what's the legal lead time?
[00:38:46] Samira: typical procurement for enterprises is 4-8 weeks depending on SOC review and DPA clauses. Since you're already on our hosted plan and we have prior security exchange, it may be closer to 4 weeks. We'll loop in our legal ops.

[00:41:12] Ava: one more on regression monitoring — can Redwood alert on quality regressions tied to prompt sets? We need to avoid silent degradation after model swaps.
[00:41:20] Nora: Yes, Redwood Optimize has eval hooks and regression alerts keyed to your prompt set. We can set thresholds and send Slack alerts. We can also store eval baselines in the console for automated comparison.

[00:45:03] Samira: Recap — action items: we'll send rightsizing scenarios (30/60/90), Liam runs a dedicated bench, Nora will set up exports and invite the exec sponsor for monthly check-ins, and Verdant will confirm budget runway. Any other asks?
[00:45:17] Priya: can you include an itemized cost delta and sensitivity to 10/20/30% growth?
[00:45:23] Samira: Yes.
[00:46:40] Mark: also include a short checklist for private deployment readiness (networking, KMS, compliance docs).
[00:46:46] Samira: Will do.

[00:49:55] Devin: small note, our infra team will share the peak window logs by tomorrow EOD.
[00:50:02] Eli: and I'll attach the eval test set for the summarization feature.
[00:50:08] Nora: Great — I'll collate and send meeting notes and the action item tracker.

[00:51:00] Samira: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the rightsizing doc and bench results. Talk soon.
[00:51:08] Ava: Thanks all.
[00:51:10] Mark: thanks.
